samples.summary: No test at all for the new `board` arm of the content endpoint (GET dispatch, PUT dispatch, `assertValidBoardBody`, `sniffBodyShape` board branch)
samples.evidence: `docs-content.controller.spec.ts` tests GET/PUT per type for doc, slides and note (e.g. line 143 'returns the note content JSON…', line 270 'writes a note body via doc.update…', line 333 shape-vs-type mismatch), but a case-insensitive grep for 'board' across packages/backend/src/api/v1 returns zero matches. So the board `docKeyPrefix: 'board-'`, `initialBoardRoot()` seeding, the `elements`-after-`slides` sniff ordering, and every branch of the ~45-line `assertValidBoardBody` (meta.title, meta.unit, meta.recentColors, per-element walk) ship untested. `board-tree.spec.ts` only covers the read/write helpers in isolation, not the controller wiring or the validator. samples.summary: New destructive PUT/GET worksheet-images controller has no spec; only the pure `parseImages` validator is tested
samples.evidence: `worksheet-images.spec.ts` covers `parseImages` thoroughly, but there is no `worksheet-images.controller.spec.ts` (glob of packages/backend/src/api/v1/*.spec.ts lists every sibling controller — tabs, charts, rules, styles, dimensions — but not this one). samples.summary: New tab delete/move/duplicate endpoints are untested at the controller level, including the `unwrapJson` proxy-detach the duplicate handler exists to do
samples.evidence: `tabs.controller.spec.ts` describes only 'ApiV1TabsController create/rename' (lines 13–160): create, rename, non-sheet documents, initialRoot seeding. Nothing exercises `remove`, `move` or `duplicate`. `tab-ops.spec.ts` covers the pure resolvers/appliers with plain objects, so what remains untested is exactly the controller-only logic: the 404/409 mapping (last_tab, pivot_dependents message listing dependents), and `duplicate`'s `unwrapJson(root.sheets?.[tabId])` — whose own comment says that without it Yorkie's `toJSON` string is stored instead of a grid, i.e. a silently corrupted duplicated tab.

samples.summary: The test named 'lists threads across every tab' uses a single-tab fixture, so the cross-tab thread walk (`tabIdOfThread`, the `tabOrder` loop in `list`) is never exercised
samples.evidence: `sheetRoot()` (spec line ~46) builds `createSpreadsheetDocument()` and only touches `sheets['tab-1']`; the test creates one thread on 'tab-1' and asserts `threads.map(t => t.id)` equals `[first.id]` — true whether or not the controller walks more than the first tab. Every other test (reply/resolve/delete) also runs against that one tab, so `tabIdOfThread` (comments.controller.ts:474) resolving a thread stored under a non-first tab is untested. That routing is the controller's central design claim ('the tab is not in the path — a thread id is unique across the document'); if it regressed, threads on any second tab would 404 on reply/resolve/delete and vanish from `list`.

samples.summary: No controller spec for the new slides controller: the 404/409 error mapping and the 'assign only root.slides' invariant are untested
samples.evidence: `slide-ops.spec.ts` covers add/duplicate/move/delete/listLayouts purely, but there is no `slides.controller.spec.ts` in packages/backend/src/api/v1. Untested: `not_found`→NotFoundException, `last_slide`→ConflictException, the slides-type guard, and the `apply()` invariant that only `root.slides` is written — which the module doc says is what stops a read→write round trip from dropping `unit`, `pxPerPt`, `slideHeight` and `recentColors` from the deck's meta.

samples.summary: The reply response's bigint→number `createdAt` conversion is untested
samples.evidence: `reply()` returns `{ ...reply, createdAt: Number(reply.createdAt) }` because `buildReply` stores a bigint (comment-ops.spec asserts `typeof thread.createdAt === 'bigint'`). The only assertion in the controller spec's reply test is `expect(reply.threadId).toBe(thread.id)` (spec line 135); nothing asserts the returned comment's `createdAt` is a finite number. If that coercion were dropped, `JSON.stringify` on a BigInt throws and every reply returns a 500 — a path no test would catch.

samples.summary: `withSref` returning a null `ref` for an orphaned anchor (deleted row/column) has no test
samples.evidence: The docblock states the derived `ref` is `null` once the anchored row or column is deleted, and that this is 'exactly how the editor tells an orphaned thread from a live one'. The spec only asserts the happy path (`ref: 'B2'` for a materialized cell, spec line ~63). No test removes an id from `rowOrder`/`colOrder` and checks the reported `ref`.

samples.summary: All new HttpClient methods are exercised only through a module-level mock, so their URLs, verbs and bodies are never asserted
samples.evidence: `vi.mock('../src/client/http-client.js', ...)` replaces the entire class, so `deleteTab`, `moveTab`, `duplicateTab`, `get/setWorksheetImages`, `listSlideLayouts`, `add/duplicate/move/deleteSlide`, the six comment methods and `get/putBoardContent` (http-client.ts:535–665) have no test hitting the real implementation. A grep for those method names across packages/cli/test matches only this mocked file; `http-client-paths.test.ts` and `http-client.test.ts` do not touch them. A wrong path (e.g. the nested `/comments/:threadId/comments/:commentId`) or wrong verb would ship and only surface as a runtime 404.

samples.summary: The new commands are tested on a hand-built command tree, and no test asserts they are mounted on the real program
samples.evidence: `run()` builds its own program (`program.command('sheets')` + direct `registerSheetsImagesCommand`/`registerSlidesEditCommand`/`registerCommentsCommand`/`registerBoardCommand`), so it passes even if `cli.ts`, `sheets.ts` or `slides.ts` never registered them. `output.test.ts:921` ('wires every namespace onto the default program') uses `expect.arrayContaining` and was not extended with 'board'/'comments'; `namespaces.test.ts` was not updated either (no `board`, `comments`, `sheets images` or `slides slide` assertions). Only `tabs.test.ts` got a registration assertion.

samples.summary: The ~16 new schema registry entries (including four new `destructive` classes) have no assertions
samples.evidence: `schema.test.ts` pins safety classes for a curated list ('safety levels match the design contract', lines 159–180) and canonical names (lines 128–153); neither was extended for `comments.*`, `board.*`, `slides.slide.*`, `sheets.tabs.delete/move/duplicate` or `sheets.images.set`. The registry is the agent-facing safety contract, so a mis-classified destructive entry (e.g. `sheets.images.set`, which deletes omitted images) would let an agent run it under write-level approval with nothing to catch it. No test verifies registry names correspond to real CLI commands either.

samples.summary: The stdin branch of `sheets images set` is untested; only `--data` is exercised
samples.evidence: class-b-commands.test.ts only invokes `sheets images set doc-1 --data '{...}'` (two tests). The `for await (const chunk of process.stdin)` branch and its error message ('… on stdin') are never run, although the command's help and the schema entry advertise piping. Comparable stdin handling elsewhere (content-write.test.ts) is tested.

samples.summary: Self-comparing assertion that collapses to `expect(false).toBe(false)` when the operation fails
samples.evidence: `expect(result.ok && result.slides[0].id).toBe(result.ok && result.id);` compares two expressions derived from the same result: if `result.ok` is false both sides are `false` and the assertion passes vacuously. The adjacent `expect(result.ok && result.index).toBe(1)` does catch a failed result, so the gap is contained, but the id assertion carries no independent information.

finding.evidence: `docs-content.controller.spec.ts` tests GET/PUT per type for doc, slides and note (e.g. line 143 'returns the note content JSON…', line 270 'writes a note body via doc.update…', line 333 shape-vs-type mismatch), but a case-insensitive grep for 'board' across packages/backend/src/api/v1 returns zero matches. So the board `docKeyPrefix: 'board-'`, `initialBoardRoot()` seeding, the `elements`-after-`slides` sniff ordering, and every branch of the ~45-line `assertValidBoardBody` (meta.title, meta.unit, meta.recentColors, per-element walk) ship untested. `board-tree.spec.ts` only covers the read/write helpers in isolation, not the controller wiring or the validator. verdict.reason: The board arm of the content endpoint genuinely has no test. The controller implements GET board dispatch (docs-content.controller.ts:139-145), PUT board dispatch with initialBoardRoot() seeding (222-233), the elements-after-slides sniff branch (264), and the ~37-line assertValidBoardBody (556-592). Only two test files import ApiV1DocsContentController: docs-content.controller.spec.ts and api-key-write-scope.guard.spec.ts (which only asserts guard mounting, line 66). docs-content.controller.spec.ts has zero case-insensitive 'board' matches; its GET/PUT dispatch tests cover doc (95), slides (121) and note (143) only, hand-written per type with no parameterized list that could include board. Searching wider for a counterexample: backend e2e specs contain only incidental 'board' strings (database.e2e-spec.ts:477 a title, document-copy-attached.e2e-spec.ts:3 a comment) with no board content roundtrip spec alongside the docs/notes ones; the CLI board test (packages/cli/test/class-b-commands.test.ts:350-388) mocks getBoardContent/putBoardContent on the HTTP client so it never reaches the controller; board-tree.spec.ts tests only the read/write/initial helpers in isolation (15-66) and yorkie-doc-key.spec.ts only the 'board-' prefix constant (75-76). Since sniffBodyShape and assertValidBoardBody are module-private, no other file can reach them. The untested path is a destructive whole-content replace, where a wrong sniff order or mis-dispatch overwrites board content through the wrong writer — data-affecting, so major.

finding.evidence: `worksheet-images.spec.ts` covers `parseImages` thoroughly, but there is no `worksheet-images.controller.spec.ts` (glob of packages/backend/src/api/v1/*.spec.ts lists every sibling controller — tabs, charts, rules, styles, dimensions — but not this one). Untested controller behavior: `setImages` wipes `ws.images = {}` and rekeys by id (an omitted image is deleted — data loss if the rekeying or the tab lookup is wrong), the `worksheetOrThrow` NotFoundException thrown *inside* `doc.update`, the sheet-type guard, and `getImages`' `unwrapJson` detach path which the code comment says is what keeps `res.json()` from blowing up on a Yorkie proxy.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: no test anywhere in the repo exercises ApiV1WorksheetImagesController. Repo-wide grep for `ApiV1WorksheetImagesController|worksheet-images.controller` (excluding node_modules) matches only api-v1.module.ts:15,59, the controller file itself, and a docs task note; grep for `setImages|getImages` across packages/ matches only the controller's own method definitions. The api/v1 spec directory holds 19 sibling specs (tabs, charts, rules, styles, dimensions, structure, cells, comments, images, ...) but none for worksheet-images. Backend e2e specs in packages/backend/test contain zero matches for `images`. The one apparent candidate elsewhere, packages/cli/test/class-b-commands.test.ts:41-62, vi.mocks the whole HttpClient and asserts only which client method is called with which args, so it cannot reach the controller. Only the pure validator is covered (packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-images.spec.ts:16-72). Untested behavior is real and destructive: setImages wipes `ws.images = {}` and rekeys by id so an omitted image is deleted (worksheet-images.controller.ts:107-108, documented at lines 28-30), worksheetOrThrow throws NotFoundException from inside doc.update (lines 53-60, 103-109), the sheet-type BadRequestException guard (lines 40-51), and getImages' unwrapJson detach path (line 81). A defect in the rekey or tab lookup silently loses user image placements, so this is a major test-adequacy gap, not a nit.

finding.summary: New tab delete/move/duplicate endpoints are untested at the controller level, including the `unwrapJson` proxy-detach the duplicate handler exists to do
finding.evidence: `tabs.controller.spec.ts` describes only 'ApiV1TabsController create/rename' (lines 13–160): create, rename, non-sheet documents, initialRoot seeding. Nothing exercises `remove`, `move` or `duplicate`. `tab-ops.spec.ts` covers the pure resolvers/appliers with plain objects, so what remains untested is exactly the controller-only logic: the 404/409 mapping (last_tab, pivot_dependents message listing dependents), and `duplicate`'s `unwrapJson(root.sheets?.[tabId])` — whose own comment says that without it Yorkie's `toJSON` string is stored instead of a grid, i.e. a silently corrupted duplicated tab.

verdict.reason: No counterexample exists. tabs.controller.spec.ts contains a single suite ('ApiV1TabsController create/rename') whose sub-suites only invoke controller.list/create/rename — including the non-sheet it.each(['list','create','rename']) and the initialRoot suite; controller.remove, controller.move and controller.duplicate are never called there or in any other file. tab-ops.spec.ts covers the resolvers/appliers with plain objects only (duplicateTab called with the plain root.sheets['tab-1'] at line 184), so it cannot exercise the controller's proxy-detach. unwrapJson (yorkie-json.ts:7) has no test at all: yorkie-json.spec.ts covers parseJsonSnapshot/normalizeJsonSnapshot/detachYorkieValue/snapshotJsonRoot only. The api-key-write-scope guard spec only asserts guard metadata on the controller class, not handler behavior. CLI tests (tabs.test.ts, class-b-commands.test.ts:165) vi.mock HttpClient, so the backend handler never executes, and no backend e2e spec references the tab delete/move/duplicate routes. Under the test-adequacy rubric this is major: the untested unwrapJson detach means a duplicated tab could silently store Yorkie's toJSON string instead of a grid (data corruption on a user path), and the 409 last_tab / pivot_dependents and 400 index mappings are controller-only logic with zero coverage.

finding.evidence: `sheetRoot()` (spec line ~46) builds `createSpreadsheetDocument()` and only touches `sheets['tab-1']`; the test creates one thread on 'tab-1' and asserts `threads.map(t => t.id)` equals `[first.id]` — true whether or not the controller walks more than the first tab. Every other test (reply/resolve/delete) also runs against that one tab, so `tabIdOfThread` (comments.controller.ts:474) resolving a thread stored under a non-first tab is untested. verdict.reason: Verified independently. `sheetRoot()` (comments.controller.spec.ts:40-46) uses `createSpreadsheetDocument()` with no args, which worksheet-document.ts:172-194 shows yields a single tab (`tabOrder: ['tab-1']`). The test 'lists threads across every tab' (spec:103-116) creates one thread on tab-1 and asserts `[first.id]`, so the `tabOrder` loop in `list` (controller.ts:133-139) runs one iteration and would pass even if it only ever read the first tab. All mutation tests (spec:118-203) use the same one-tab fixture, so `tabIdOfThread` (controller.ts:474-483), the resolver behind reply/resolve/delete via `mutateMap` (controller.ts:327), is never exercised for a thread stored under a non-first tab. I searched wide for a counterexample and found none: comment-ops.spec.ts tests the tab-agnostic map helpers only; packages/cli/test/class-b-commands.test.ts mocks the HTTP client entirely (its tab-2 usages are in the `sheets tabs` block); no backend e2e spec exercises the comments API; and no file other than api-v1.module.ts, the controller and its spec references ApiV1CommentsController. Blocking under the test-adequacy rubric: a misleadingly named test presented as cross-tab coverage over a new user-facing route whose failure would 404 threads on any second tab and drop them from list.
